extracted.intended_audience: NIH program staff, policymakers, and early-career investigators
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and programmatic priorities governing NIH prioritization of Early Stage Investigators (ESI) and Early Established Investigators (EEI), including definitions of career-stage windows, the threshold for what counts as a 'substantial' R01-equivalent, implementation targets, and accountability mechanisms. Useful for designing or evaluating grant-funding decisions and programmatic rubrics at NIH Institutes/Centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Stage Investigator (ESI) status
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PI within 10 years of completing terminal research degree (or end of post-graduate clinical training, whichever is later) AND has NOT previously competed successfully as PD/PI for substantial NIH independent research award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESIs are prioritized for funding — meritorious ESI applications receive extra consideration (programmatic priority can be used to fund ESIs above the score-based payline). The 10-year window is measured from terminal degree or end of clinical training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Established Investigator (EEI) status
rubrics_metrics.description: An investigator within 10 years of receiving their first substantial NIH R01-equivalent award as an ESI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EEIs are prioritized for funding in specific circumstances — e.g., if losing all R01 support or if only one award remains. The EEI window is defined relative to the date of the investigator's first substantial R01-equivalent award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Established Investigator
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Established Investigators are processed under the standard review and funding decision procedures (i.e., no special ESI/EEI programmatic priority applies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'substantial' R01-equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH's definition of competitively-substantial-equivalent includes specific grant mechanisms (R01, R37, DP1, DP2, DP5, R23, R29, R35), total direct costs above specified thresholds, and multi-year duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy contains the detailed thresholds and duration criteria; the substantive mechanisms listed are considered R01-equivalent for the purpose of determining prior independent support and eligibility for ESI/EEI status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform goals (values guiding prioritization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary goals driving the NGRI: (1) mitigate workforce aging by reversing rising mean age of first R01 receipt, (2) promote earlier research independence for new investigators, (3) stabilize careers of early-established investigators at risk of attrition, (4) provide statutory implementation of the 21st Century Cures Act mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These values justify programmatic priority for ESIs/EEIs and should be treated as explicit objectives when setting targets and assessing impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute/Center (IC) ESI funding goals (quantified targets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each NIH Institute/Center sets explicit ESI funding goals (initially framed as 200+ MORE ESI awards than FY2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets are numeric and IC-specific; quantification enables management attention and allocation of programmatic resources to meet goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic authority to fund ESIs above score-based payline
rubrics_metrics.description: Program staff have explicit authority to fund ESI applications above the standard score-based payline as a mechanism to prioritize early-career investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a programmatic override applied at the funding-decision stage — it does not change per-application peer review scoring criteria but affects which scored applications receive awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking and public reporting of ESI funding rates (audit/accountability)
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI funding rates are tracked and reported as an accountability metric for the initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditing and public reporting create transparency and enable evaluation of whether ICs meet their ESI funding goals; tracking metrics should be specified and monitored regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary programmatic priorities applied at funding-decision stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatic priorities (career stage, demographic representation, geographic distribution, topic balance, etc.) can be applied when selecting among scored applications without changing the underlying review scoring rubric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designing a funding rubric can separate per-application scoring criteria from programmatic priorities; the latter can be statutory, quantified, audited, and transparent, and should be explicitly documented to avoid hidden trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design features of the NGRI (statutory/quantified/audited/transparent)
rubrics_metrics.description: NGRI is characterized as statutory (mandated by Congress), quantified (specific numerical goals per IC), audited (tracking and reporting of ESI funding rates), and transparent (the priority is explicitly stated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These design features are presented as reasons for the initiative's robustness and replicability; rubric designers may aim to emulate these attributes to strengthen programmatic priorities.
